chunk_findings.detail: The change makes `item_edit` the single `ItemEdit` encoder for both the MCP call and `ddflow update`, but it drops the one piece of CLI-side normalization that the old CLI path relied on. `update_message.py` deletes `csv_or_none`, whose docstring states the CLI contract explicitly: "`None` stays None (leave alone); a string is a comma list." In the new shared builder the non-glob list fields route through `_list_or_none` (visible just above line 23: `return None if v is None else list(v) if isinstance(v, list) else [v]`), which wraps a scalar string as a *single element* and never splits on commas. Concretely, `ddflow update ISSUE-1 --needs a,b` now yields `ItemEdit(needs=["a,b"])` — one need literally named `a,b` — whereas the CLI path previously produced `["a","b"]` via `csv_or_none`. The same applies to `add_needs`, `remove_needs`, `add_tags`, `remove_tags`, `tags` and `resources`. Note the asymmetry the diff itself preserves: only `globs`/`add_globs`/`remove_globs` get comma splitting (`_raw_globs`, "split on commas here first"), which is exactly the CLI-string case the other list fields now lack. So unifying the two call sites into "the ONE encoding" is only correct if both callers hand `item_edit` identically-shaped values; if the CLI still passes its parsed comma strings (which is what `csv_or_none` existed to consume), the refactor silently changes the meaning of every list argument on the CLI, the very class of "field threaded through one path but not the other" the change is meant to eliminate. Either the CLI must normalize with `csv_list` before building the dict, or `item_edit` must split comma strings for these fields as it already does for globs.

chunk_findings.detail: `apply` documents `abandon` (id -> reason) as part of its contract ("abandon the items in `abandon` ..., all or nothing"), and `apply` even threads it into `_plan(cfg, st, entries, abandon, kind)` — but `_plan` never looks at it. The only ids that get validated (existence, not removed, not terminal, not duplicated) are the `entries`; the abandon ids are used raw. `_record` then does `ab = st.items[iid]` unguarded. So a caller of the shared engine that passes an id that is not in state, e.g. `ddflow.api.batch.apply(repo, [], abandon={"B404": "dup"})`, raises `KeyError` from inside `with log.transaction():` instead of returning the `O.failed`/`O.refused` outcome every other bad input produces. Note the placement: the raise happens in the abandon loop, i.e. *after* the `log.append(f"{it.family}.updated", ...)` events and lease retargets for the whole batch have already been written, so if `log.transaction()` is a lock rather than a rollback-able unit the "a refusal anywhere records nothing" / all-or-nothing property is broken (half the batch persisted and the process dies). The same gap lets an id that is also present in `entries` be updated and abandoned in the same transaction, and lets an already-removed/terminal item be abandoned again; `_plan`'s unused `abandon` parameter is exactly where that validation was meant to go. (Reachable through the Python API and any surface that forwards an abandon list; the `fold` path happens to pre-validate `dup`, which is why the tests do not see it.)

chunk_findings.detail: The `task fold` command declares `payload=("dup", "keep", "repointed", "dry_run", "edits", "abandoned")`, omitting `"unchanged"`, but its renderer `fold_text` tail-calls `batch_text`, which does `if d["unchanged"]:` and `', '.join(d['unchanged'])`. chunk_findings.detail: The batch is planned and the cycle check is performed in `apply` *before* any lock is taken; only `_record` enters `log.transaction()`. Two concurrent `ddflow update --batch` (or `task fold`) runs therefore both plan against the same cycle-free snapshot, both pass `_cycle_refusal`, and then serialise their appends under the lock, so the check the feature promises ("a cycle check ... in one locked transaction") cannot see the other writer's committed edges. Interleaving: batch 1 sets `A.needs=[B]`, batch 2 sets `B.needs=[A]`; each is acyclic against the pre-batch graph, both are accepted, and the committed log ends with A→B→A — exactly the cycle the check is supposed to refuse. The same staleness also causes lost updates: because the `.updated` event carries the *full* resolved field list computed from the pre-lock snapshot (e.g. `needs`), a second batch planned before the first commits overwrites the first batch's list instead of merging/refusing. Re-planning (or at least re-running `_cycle_refusal`) inside the transaction, against the state read under the lock, is required for the stated guarantee.

chunk_findings.detail: `abandon` is never validated: `_plan` accepts the parameter and ignores it, while `_record` does `ab = st.items[iid]` for every key. `apply` is the documented engine for every surface, so any caller passing an id that is not a live item either raises `KeyError` mid-transaction (`apply(repo, [], abandon={"nope": "x"})`) or, if the id names an already-terminal item, happily appends `item.abandoned` and releases the lease of a done task. `fold` happens to pre-validate, so this is a latent API hole rather than a fold failure, but the abandon ids should be checked for existence/terminality alongside the per-entry checks in `_plan`.

chunk_findings.detail: `fold`'s declared `payload` is `("dup", "keep", "repointed", "dry_run", "edits", "abandoned")`, but its renderer `fold_text` delegates to `batch_text`, which unconditionally reads `d["unchanged"]` (`if d["unchanged"]: ...` in `batch_text`). `batch`'s own payload — the list of keys the surface declares/returns — does include `"unchanged"`, so the engine's fold result and the declared fold payload are inconsistent: running `ddflow task fold DUP KEEP` (or `ddflow_task_fold`) either raises `KeyError: 'unchanged'` in the render path when the payload is used to build `out.data`, or silently drops the "unchanged" section of the fold report that `batch_text` is written to emit. The engine is shared with `batch` (whose payload lists all four keys the renderer touches), so the fold payload is the one missing a key its own renderer dereferences; the fix is to add `"unchanged"` to the fold payload (or guard the access).

chunk_findings.detail: The change makes the fold hard-refuse when the duplicate carries a live lease from another holder (`run_cli(repo, "claim", "B", "--agent", "w")` then `task fold B A` ⇒ exit 3, `"claimed"` in stderr, nothing recorded), and no CONTESTED record or resolution path is produced. Concretely: with B leased by agent `w`, folding B into A aborts with exit 3 and both the log and `doctor` show nothing, so the conflicting lease is neither surfaced to `next`/`doctor` nor resolvable via `ddflow resolve B --keep ...`; the only way out is for the operator to know out-of-band who holds the lease and wait, which is exactly the state the decision says must be recorded as CONTESTED and settled on the record.

chunk_findings.detail:
The guard is written as `if retargets:` *before* `L.plan_retarget` is called for the current item, and the previous item is appended to `retargets` unconditionally (`retargets.append((it, lease, globs, res))`), whether or not it actually has a lease (the later loop proves `lease` can be `None`: `for it, lease, globs, res in retargets: if lease is not None: ...`). `plan_retarget` on an unclaimed item returns `(None, None)` — there is nothing to retarget — so a batch that edits globs/resources on two items that hold **no** lease is refused at the second entry with "the batch retargets more than one lease (A already); change one *claimed* item's globs or resources per batch", even though neither item is claimed and no lease is involved. Input that demonstrates it: `ddflow update --batch FILE` where FILE contains `{"id": "A", "globs": ["x/**"]}` and `{"id": "B", "globs": ["y/**"]}` for two leased-nowhere tasks; A passes `plan_retarget` (lease `None`), B hits `if retargets:` and the whole batch is refused and recorded. This contradicts the change's own rationale (the comment and message are about *leases* "as they are NOW", and the guard should only trip on entries whose `lease is not None`) and it defeats the stated use case of bulk "globs add/remove" in one transaction — the only workaround is splitting into one-item batches, which loses atomicity. The fix is to test for an already-planned real lease (e.g. `if any(l is not None for _, l, _, _ in retargets):`) rather than for any prior candidate.

(Previous finding 1 on `_plan`/abandon is answered by this diff: the `for iid in abandon:` block now validates existence/removed/terminal/claimed before `_record` reaches `st.items[iid]`. Previous finding 2 is in `ddflow/surfaces/declared/batch.py`, which is not in this part, so it cannot be verified from this delta.)

chunk_findings.detail: `apply` documents `abandon` (id -> reason) as part of its contract ("abandon the items in `abandon` ..., all or nothing"), and `apply` even threads it into `_plan(cfg, st, entries, abandon, kind)` — but `_plan` never looks at it. The only ids that get validated (existence, not removed, not terminal, not duplicated) are the `entries`; the abandon ids are used raw. `_record` then does `ab = st.items[iid]` unguarded. So a caller of the shared engine that passes an id that is not in state, e.g. `ddflow.api.batch.apply(repo, [], abandon={"B404": "dup"})`, raises `KeyError` from inside `with log.transaction():` instead of returning the `O.failed`/`O.refused` outcome every other bad input produces. Note the placement: the raise happens in the abandon loop, i.e. *after* the `log.append(f"{it.family}.updated", ...)` events and lease retargets for the whole batch have already been written, so if `log.transaction()` is a lock rather than a rollback-able unit the "a refusal anywhere records nothing" / all-or-nothing property is broken (half the batch persisted and the process dies). The same gap lets an id that is also present in `entries` be updated and abandoned in the same transaction, and lets an already-removed/terminal item be abandoned again; `_plan`'s unused `abandon` parameter is exactly where that validation was meant to go. (Reachable through the Python API and any surface that forwards an abandon list; the `fold` path happens to pre-validate `dup`, which is why the tests do not see it.)

chunk_findings.detail: The `task fold` command declares `payload=("dup", "keep", "repointed", "dry_run", "edits", "abandoned")`, omitting `"unchanged"`, but its renderer `fold_text` tail-calls `batch_text`, which does `if d["unchanged"]:` and `', '.join(d['unchanged'])`. Running a successful `ddflow task fold DUP KEEP` therefore renders through a key the fold result declares it does not have (and which the `batch` command, by contrast, does declare), so the projection/render path raises `KeyError: 'unchanged'` on the very case the command exists for. Either `"unchanged"` must be added to the fold payload (and produced by `api/batch.fold`) or `batch_text` must treat the key as optional when rendering a fold.

chunk_findings.detail:
The guard is written as `if retargets:` *before* `L.plan_retarget` is called for the current item, and the previous item is appended to `retargets` unconditionally (`retargets.append((it, lease, globs, res))`), whether or not it actually has a lease (the later loop proves `lease` can be `None`: `for it, lease, globs, res in retargets: if lease is not None: ...`). `plan_retarget` on an unclaimed item returns `(None, None)` — there is nothing to retarget — so a batch that edits globs/resources on two items that hold **no** lease is refused at the second entry with "the batch retargets more than one lease (A already); change one *claimed* item's globs or resources per batch", even though neither item is claimed and no lease is involved. Input that demonstrates it: `ddflow update --batch FILE` where FILE contains `{"id": "A", "globs": ["x/**"]}` and `{"id": "B", "globs": ["y/**"]}` for two leased-nowhere tasks; A passes `plan_retarget` (lease `None`), B hits `if retargets:` and the whole batch is refused and recorded. This contradicts the change's own rationale (the comment and message are about *leases* "as they are NOW", and the guard should only trip on entries whose `lease is not None`) and it defeats the stated use case of bulk "globs add/remove" in one transaction — the only workaround is splitting into one-item batches, which loses atomicity. The fix is to test for an already-planned real lease (e.g. `if any(l is not None for _, l, _, _ in retargets):`) rather than for any prior candidate.

(Previous finding 1 on `_plan`/abandon is answered by this diff: the `for iid in abandon:` block now validates existence/removed/terminal/claimed before `_record` reaches `st.items[iid]`. Previous finding 2 is in `ddflow/surfaces/declared/batch.py`, which is not in this part, so it cannot be verified from this delta.)

chunk_findings.detail: The batch is planned and the cycle check is performed in `apply` *before* any lock is taken; only `_record` enters `log.transaction()`. Two concurrent `ddflow update --batch` (or `task fold`) runs therefore both plan against the same cycle-free snapshot, both pass `_cycle_refusal`, and then serialise their appends under the lock, so the check the feature promises ("a cycle check ... in one locked transaction") cannot see the other writer's committed edges. Interleaving: batch 1 sets `A.needs=[B]`, batch 2 sets `B.needs=[A]`; each is acyclic against the pre-batch graph, both are accepted, and the committed log ends with A→B→A — exactly the cycle the check is supposed to refuse. The same staleness also causes lost updates: because the `.updated` event carries the *full* resolved field list computed from the pre-lock snapshot (e.g. `needs`), a second batch planned before the first commits overwrites the first batch's list instead of merging/refusing. Re-planning (or at least re-running `_cycle_refusal`) inside the transaction, against the state read under the lock, is required for the stated guarantee.

chunk_findings.detail: `abandon` is never validated: `_plan` accepts the parameter and ignores it, while `_record` does `ab = st.items[iid]` for every key. `apply` is the documented engine for every surface, so any caller passing an id that is not a live item either raises `KeyError` mid-transaction (`apply(repo, [], abandon={"nope": "x"})`) or, if the id names an already-terminal item, happily appends `item.abandoned` and releases the lease of a done task. `fold` happens to pre-validate, so this is a latent API hole rather than a fold failure, but the abandon ids should be checked for existence/terminality alongside the per-entry checks in `_plan`.

chunk_findings.detail: `fold`'s declared `payload` is `("dup", "keep", "repointed", "dry_run", "edits", "abandoned")`, but its renderer `fold_text` delegates to `batch_text`, which unconditionally reads `d["unchanged"]` (`if d["unchanged"]: ...` in `batch_text`). `batch`'s own payload — the list of keys the surface declares/returns — does include `"unchanged"`, so the engine's fold result and the declared fold payload are inconsistent: running `ddflow task fold DUP KEEP` (or `ddflow_task_fold`) either raises `KeyError: 'unchanged'` in the render path when the payload is used to build `out.data`, or silently drops the "unchanged" section of the fold report that `batch_text` is written to emit. The engine is shared with `batch` (whose payload lists all four keys the renderer touches), so the fold payload is the one missing a key its own renderer dereferences; the fix is to add `"unchanged"` to the fold payload (or guard the access).
